title: Release v0.2.0: bump VERSION, fix unresolvable @v1 ref
description:
Tracks GH #36 (https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-sync/issues/36). 35 commits since v0.1.1.

Two things must land in the tagged commit. (1) @v1 does not resolve — no v1 tag or branch exists, only v0.1.0/v0.1.1 — yet README, the Marketplace listing and docs/quickstart/workflows all tell users 'uses: SteerSpec/strspc-sync/sync@v1'. Anyone copying the quickstart got a workflow error. Pre-1.0, so point docs at @v0.2.0 rather than inventing a floating v1 that promises stability the project is not offering. (2) The four composite actions read the VERSION file to build the binary download URL, so VERSION must say 0.2.0 in the commit being tagged — tagging first would publish v0.2.0 whose actions download v0.1.1 binaries.
acceptance_criteria: VERSION reads 0.2.0; no @v1 references remain; merged to main; tag v0.2.0 pushed and release.yml green; the published release archives contain LICENSE + NOTICE; gh release list shows v0.2.0 as Latest.
close_reason: Released v0.2.0. PR #37 merged as f376cde, tagged and published; download URL, checksum, archive contents and version string all verified against the live release.

title: getBaseSHA returns a branch name, not a SHA
description: Tracks GH #31 (https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-sync/issues/31). internal/sync/sync.go:405 calls Repos.GetDefaultBranch, which returns the branch NAME (repos.go:79), and passes it to CreateBranch as baseSHA -- POSTed to git/refs as 'sha', so the real API answers 422. Invisible because sync.go discards the error with '_ ='. Fix: add RepoService.GetBranchSHA against GET /repos/{o}/{r}/git/ref/heads/{branch}; use it in getBaseSHA; tolerate only 422 (already-exists) from CreateBranch via *gh.APIError StatusCode and surface anything else as an error. Interface addition breaks all three mockRepoService impls (sync/monitor/conflict tests).
acceptance_criteria: GetBranchSHA covered in internal/github/client_test.go; sync_test.go covers 422-tolerated vs hard-failure branch creation; go test -race ./... passes; coverage stays >= 70%.
close_reason: Merged to main: PR #33 (c6fb1d7), PR #34 (1a6915e), PR #35 (a9b032c). GH #29/#30/#31 closed with summary comments.

title: Quickstart example config fails to load
description: Tracks GH #30 (https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-sync/issues/30). docs/quickstart/steerspec-sync.yml -- the config the README points every new user at -- does not parse: line 29 nests a list (managed_sections) under a template's variables, but TemplateConfig.Variables is map[string]string (internal/config/config.go:39). managed_sections is referenced nowhere in Go; renderMarker ignores variables entirely, so the key is aspirational -- remove it rather than widening the type. Second defect hidden behind the first: no template carries the version field that config.Validate requires as semver (config.go:167). Add version 1.0.0 to all four.
acceptance_criteria: strspc sync --config docs/quickstart/steerspec-sync.yml --dry-run gets past config load; regression test in internal/config/config_test.go loads the shipped example and asserts no error.
close_reason: Merged to main: PR #33 (c6fb1d7), PR #34 (1a6915e), PR #35 (a9b032c). GH #29/#30/#31 closed with summary comments.

title: [epic] Relicense to Apache 2.0 + public repo polish
description:
Tracks GH issue #29 (https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-sync/issues/29).

strspc-sync ships MIT while every other public SteerSpec repo is Apache 2.0 (strspc-manager, strspc-rules, strspc-pr-review). MIT was an oversight. Relicense is clean: single contributor (PLB, 37 commits), copyright already held by SteerSpec, no third-party consent needed.

Also closes three presentation gaps on a repo that is public AND Marketplace-listed: empty GitHub description/topics/homepage, a README with no badges, and no community health files.

Covers: LICENSE + NOTICE + .goreleaser.yml archive files; README badges and structure; repo metadata via gh repo edit; CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY/CODEOWNERS.
acceptance_criteria: gh repo view --json licenseInfo reports apache-2.0; NOTICE present in release archive; all 5 README badges render; repo description/homepage/topics set; pre-commit run --all-files passes.
close_reason: Merged to main: PR #33 (c6fb1d7), PR #34 (1a6915e), PR #35 (a9b032c). GH #29/#30/#31 closed with summary comments.

title: Drop Codecov, enforce coverage natively in CI
description:
Tracks GH #32 (https://github.com/SteerSpec/strspc-sync/issues/32). Re-scoped from 'fix the silent Codecov upload' after an org-wide check: strspc-sync is the ONLY repo in SteerSpec wired to Codecov, and its upload has never landed (badge reads 'unknown'). strspc-CLI generates coverage.out and never reads it; strspc-manager has no coverage; strspc-rules none. Codecov was a one-off that failed silently, not a convention — so repairing it would mean taking on a third-party dependency, a secret to rotate and an external failure point to get what go tool cover already provides in the same run.

Done: removed the codecov-action step; dropped pull-requests: write from the test job (it existed only for Codecov PR comments); moved the threshold to a THRESHOLD env var; wrote the total plus a collapsible per-function breakdown to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY so the number is visible without opening logs; kept coverage.out as a build artifact. No badge — nothing authoritative to point it at, and a hardcoded percentage goes stale silently.
acceptance_criteria: CODECOV_TOKEN secret exists; ci.yml passes the token and sets fail_ci_if_error: true; a CI run on main uploads successfully; badge renders a real percentage (~83%) not 'unknown'; README badge block updated.
close_reason: PR #40 merged (8157bc1). Codecov removed; coverage enforced natively via go tool cover with the total in the run summary. pull-requests: write dropped from the test job. Copilot's pipefail note hardened in 4ea3a5e.
